candidate.cve_desc: The retr.c:fd_read_body() function is called when processing OK responses. When the response is sent chunked in wget before 1.19.2, the chunk parser uses strtol() to read each chunk's length, but doesn't check that the chunk length is a non-negative number. The code then tries to read the chunk in pieces of 8192 bytes by using the MIN() macro, but ends up passing the negative chunk length to retr.c:fd_read(). As fd_read() takes an int argument, the high 32 bits of the chunk length are discarded, leaving fd_read() with a completely attacker controlled length argument. The attacker can corrupt malloc metadata after the allocated buffer.

target.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. In affeced versions during execution, `EinsumHelper::ParseEquation()` is supposed to set the flags in `input_has_ellipsis` vector and `*output_has_ellipsis` boolean to indicate whether there is ellipsis in the corresponding inputs and output. candidate.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the code for `tf.raw_ops.SaveV2` does not properly validate the inputs and an attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/8d72537c6abf5a44103b57b9c2e22c14f5f49698/tensorflow/core/kernels/save_restore_v2_ops.cc) uses `ValidateInputs` to check that the input arguments are valid. This validation would have caught the illegal state represented by the reproducer above. However, the validation uses `OP_REQUIRES` which translates to setting the `Status` object of the current `OpKernelContext` to an error status, followed by an empty `return` statement which just terminates the execution of the function it is present in. However, this does not mean that the kernel execution is finalized: instead, execution continues from the next line in `Compute` that follows the call to `ValidateInputs`. This is equivalent to lacking the validation. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 9728c60e136912a12d99ca56e106b7cce7af5986. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

candidate.cve_desc: ASN.1 strings are represented internally within OpenSSL as an ASN1_STRING structure which contains a buffer holding the string data and a field holding the buffer length. This contrasts with normal C strings which are repesented as a buffer for the string data which is terminated with a NUL (0) byte. Although not a strict requirement, ASN.1 strings that are parsed using OpenSSL's own "d2i" functions (and other similar parsing functions) as well as any string whose value has been set with the ASN1_STRING_set() function will additionally NUL terminate the byte array in the ASN1_STRING structure. However, it is possible for applications to directly construct valid ASN1_STRING structures which do not NUL terminate the byte array by directly setting the "data" and "length" fields in the ASN1_STRING array. This can also happen by using the ASN1_STRING_set0() function. Numerous OpenSSL functions that print ASN.1 data have been found to assume that the ASN1_STRING byte array will be NUL terminated, even though this is not guaranteed for strings that have been directly constructed. Where an application requests an ASN.1 structure to be printed, and where that ASN.1 structure contains ASN1_STRINGs that have been directly constructed by the application without NUL terminating the "data" field, then a read buffer overrun can occur. The same thing can also occur during name constraints processing of certificates (for example if a certificate has been directly constructed by the application instead of loading it via the OpenSSL parsing functions, and the certificate contains non NUL terminated ASN1_STRING structures). It can also occur in the X509_get1_email(), X509_REQ_get1_email() and X509_get1_ocsp() functions. If a malicious actor can cause an application to directly construct an ASN1_STRING and then process it through one of the affected OpenSSL functions then this issue could be hit. This might result in a crash (causing a Denial of Service attack). It could also result in the disclosure of private memory contents (such as private keys, or sensitive plaintext). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1l (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1k). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2za (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2y).

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in the IPv6 protocol specification, related to ICMP Packet Too Big (PTB) messages. (The scope of this CVE is all affected IPv6 implementations from all vendors.) The security implications of IP fragmentation have been discussed at length in [RFC6274] and [RFC7739]. An attacker can leverage the generation of IPv6 atomic fragments to trigger the use of fragmentation in an arbitrary IPv6 flow (in scenarios in which actual fragmentation of packets is not needed) and can subsequently perform any type of fragmentation-based attack against legacy IPv6 nodes that do not implement [RFC6946]. That is, employing fragmentation where not actually needed allows for fragmentation-based attack vectors to be employed, unnecessarily. We note that, unfortunately, even nodes that already implement [RFC6946] can be subject to DoS attacks as a result of the generation of IPv6 atomic fragments. Let us assume that Host A is communicating with Host B and that, as a result of the widespread dropping of IPv6 packets that contain extension headers (including fragmentation) [RFC7872], some intermediate node filters fragments between Host B and Host A. If an attacker sends a forged ICMPv6 PTB error message to Host B, reporting an MTU smaller than 1280, this will trigger the generation of IPv6 atomic fragments from that moment on (as required by [RFC2460]). When Host B starts sending IPv6 atomic fragments (in response to the received ICMPv6 PTB error message), these packets will be dropped, since we previously noted that IPv6 packets with extension headers were being dropped between Host B and Host A. Thus, this situation will result in a DoS scenario. Another possible scenario is that in which two BGP peers are employing IPv6 transport and they implement Access Control Lists (ACLs) to drop IPv6 fragments (to avoid control-plane attacks). If the aforementioned BGP peers drop IPv6 fragments but still honor received ICMPv6 PTB error messages, an attacker could easily attack the corresponding peering session by simply sending an ICMPv6 PTB message with a reported MTU smaller than 1280 bytes. Once the attack packet has been sent, the aforementioned routers will themselves be the ones dropping their own traffic.

target.cve_desc: Puma is a HTTP 1.1 server for Ruby/Rack applications. Prior to versions 5.5.1 and 4.3.9, using `puma` with a proxy which forwards HTTP header values which contain the LF character could allow HTTP request smugggling. A client could smuggle a request through a proxy, causing the proxy to send a response back to another unknown client. The only proxy which has this behavior, as far as the Puma team is aware of, is Apache Traffic Server. If the proxy uses persistent connections and the client adds another request in via HTTP pipelining, the proxy may mistake it as the first request's body. Puma, however, would see it as two requests, and when processing the second request, send back a response that the proxy does not expect. If the proxy has reused the persistent connection to Puma to send another request for a different client, the second response from the first client will be sent to the second client. This vulnerability was patched in Puma 5.5.1 and 4.3.9. As a workaround, do not use Apache Traffic Server with `puma`.

audit.reason: Only broad CWE/theme overlap; no mechanism-level alignment.

We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.6.1, TensorFlow 2.5.2, and TensorFlow 2.4.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

candidate.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions it is possible to nest a `tf.map_fn` within another `tf.map_fn` call. However, if the input tensor is a `RaggedTensor` and there is no function signature provided, code assumes the output is a fully specified tensor and fills output buffer with uninitialized contents from the heap. The `t` and `z` outputs should be identical, however this is not the case. The last row of `t` contains data from the heap which can be used to leak other memory information. The bug lies in the conversion from a `Variant` tensor to a `RaggedTensor`. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/ragged_tensor_from_variant_op.cc#L177-L190) does not check that all inner shapes match and this results in the additional dimensions. The same implementation can result in data loss, if input tensor is tweaked. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 4e2565483d0ffcadc719bd44893fb7f609bb5f12. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

candidate.cve_desc: Maddy Mail Server is an open source SMTP compatible email server. candidate.cve_desc: Node.js versions before 10.23.1, 12.20.1, 14.15.4, 15.5.1 allow two copies of a header field in an HTTP request (for example, two Transfer-Encoding header fields). In this case, Node.js identifies the first header field and ignores the second. This can lead to HTTP Request Smuggling.

target.cve_desc: Puma is a HTTP 1.1 server for Ruby/Rack applications. Prior to versions 5.5.1 and 4.3.9, using `puma` with a proxy which forwards HTTP header values which contain the LF character could allow HTTP request smugggling. A client could smuggle a request through a proxy, causing the proxy to send a response back to another unknown client. The only proxy which has this behavior, as far as the Puma team is aware of, is Apache Traffic Server. If the proxy uses persistent connections and the client adds another request in via HTTP pipelining, the proxy may mistake it as the first request's body. Puma, however, would see it as two requests, and when processing the second request, send back a response that the proxy does not expect. If the proxy has reused the persistent connection to Puma to send another request for a different client, the second response from the first client will be sent to the second client. This vulnerability was patched in Puma 5.5.1 and 4.3.9. As a workaround, do not use Apache Traffic Server with `puma`.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both target and candidate address HTTP request smuggling caused by improper handling of HTTP header values/fields, specifically allowing malformed or duplicate headers to be interpreted inconsistently.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target: LF in header value bypasses parser; Candidate: duplicate Transfer-Encoding headers cause first to be used and second ignored. Both violate the invariant that header parsing must be unambiguous and reject or normalize malformed/duplicate headers.
audit.transferable_principle: The candidate repair demonstrates the principle of resetting parser state when a duplicate header is encountered to prevent smuggling, which is directly analogous to the target's need to reject invalid characters in header values.
audit.reason: Both fixes address the same immediate failed safety condition: HTTP request smuggling due to inconsistent header parsing, making the candidate a direct mechanism-level reference.

candidate.cve_desc: Integer overflow in the MallocFrameBuffer function in vncviewer.c in LibVNCServer 0.9.9 and earlier allows remote VNC servers to cause a denial of service (crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via an advertisement for a large screen size, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

hypothesis.operation: allocation of decoded pixel buffer and row pointer table
hypothesis.trigger_condition: w and h pass cMaxPNGSize but their product overflows unsigned int
hypothesis.violated_invariant: imagesize and h * sizeof(png_bytep) must fit in unsigned int and represent the actual allocation size
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: Multiplying width and height before allocation can wrap to a small value, causing an undersized pixel buffer.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Use checked 64-bit arithmetic or a size limit that prevents w*h*4 from overflowing the allocation type.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check cMaxPNGSize and the type of imagesize to determine whether w*h*4 can wrap before new unsigned char[imagesize].

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both are integer overflow in allocation size arithmetic before buffer allocation.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis: w*h*4 overflows unsigned int; candidate: width*height*bitsPerPixel/8 overflows before malloc.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate directly shows the same repair: promote to 64-bit, check against SIZE_MAX, then allocate.
audit.reason: Strict same failed safety condition: unchecked multiplication overflow in allocation size.

candidate.cve_desc: In avrc_msg_cback of avrc_api.cc, there is a possible out-of-bound read due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to remote information disclosure over Bluetooth with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-7.0 Android-7.1.1 Android-7.1.2 Android-8.0 Android-8.1 Android-9.0 Android ID: A-111803925

hypothesis.operation: reading fcTL frame dimensions from chunk payload
hypothesis.trigger_condition: chunk.size is less than 34 bytes when fcTL fields are read
hypothesis.violated_invariant: chunk.size must be at least 34 before reading bytes at offsets 12 through 33
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: fcTL fields are dereferenced without a visible check that the chunk payload contains the required 34 bytes.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard fcTL processing with a chunk.size >= 34 check before reading frame geometry and timing fields.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Inspect read_chunk and any fcTL-specific size validation to confirm whether chunk.size is guaranteed to be 34.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve reading fixed-size fields from a packet/chunk payload without first verifying that the payload is large enough, leading to out-of-bounds read.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: The hypothesis requires chunk.size >= 34 before reading fcTL fields; the candidate adds p_pkt->len < AVRC_AVC_HDR_SIZE and similar length checks before parsing fixed-size fields.
audit.transferable_principle: The candidate demonstrates the exact repair pattern: check the remaining payload length against the required fixed-size header before dereferencing.
audit.reason: Same immediate failed safety condition: missing length check before reading fixed-size fields from a packet payload.

candidate.cve_desc: A WebPImage::decodeChunks integer overflow in Exiv2 through 0.27.1 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (large heap allocation followed by a very long running loop) via a crafted WEBP image file.

hypothesis.operation: rewriting fdAT chunk header in place
hypothesis.trigger_condition: chunk.size is less than 16 when the fdAT length field is written
hypothesis.violated_invariant: chunk.size must be at least 16 before writing the 4-byte length at offset 4 and the IDAT type at offset 8
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The fdAT branch writes into the chunk buffer without a visible minimum-size check for the fdAT header.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Validate chunk.size >= 16 before converting fdAT to IDAT in place.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check read_chunk and fdAT handling to see whether chunk.size is guaranteed to be at least 16 before the in-place rewrite.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve parsing chunked data and validating that a chunk size is sufficient before using it, but the candidate's immediate failure is an integer overflow in chunk size handling rather than an in-place header rewrite.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Candidate enforces size <= filesize - tell and uses readOrThrow, which is a related but not identical invariant to ensuring chunk.size >= 16 before writing at offsets 4 and 8.
audit.transferable_principle: The candidate demonstrates the principle of validating chunk size against remaining file extent before processing, which is transferable to checking chunk.size >= 16 before in-place fdAT-to-IDAT conversion.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure (integer overflow vs. insufficient header size) but supplies a concrete transferable verification principle for chunk size validation.

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.2.3. Out of bounds access exists in the functions ath6kl_wmi_pstream_timeout_event_rx and ath6kl_wmi_cac_event_rx in the file drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath6kl/wmi.c.

hypothesis.operation: dereference of a scalar tensor element
hypothesis.trigger_condition: handle tensor has zero elements or an unexpected shape
hypothesis.violated_invariant: handle tensor must contain at least one scalar element before scalar access
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The scalar accessor indexes the handle tensor without proving that the tensor contains a scalar element.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the scalar access by checking that the handle tensor has exactly one element before dereferencing it.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether the handle tensor shape and element count are validated before handle.scalar<tstring>()() is evaluated.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns unchecked scalar access on a tensor; candidate repair adds a bounds check on an index before use.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis trigger is zero-element or unexpected-shape handle tensor; candidate trigger is out-of-range AC value in WMI event.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate demonstrates validating an index/field against a known bound before dereference, which is a concrete transferable verification principle for the scalar-access hypothesis.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but provides a concrete bounds-validation principle relevant to checking element/index validity before access.

candidate.cve_desc: OMXCodec.cpp in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-09-01, and 7.0 before 2016-09-01 does not validate a certain pointer, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (device hang or reboot) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 29421811.

hypothesis.operation: deletion of a session tensor by name
hypothesis.trigger_condition: name does not identify an existing tensor or identifies a tensor in an invalid state
hypothesis.violated_invariant: name must refer to a valid, deletable session tensor before deletion
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The code passes a caller-supplied tensor name to DeleteTensor without locally proving that the name resolves to a valid deletable tensor.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Ensure DeleteTensor validates name resolution and returns a distinguishable error for missing or invalid tensor names.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Inspect DeleteTensor to confirm whether it checks name presence, tensor type, and deletion eligibility before removing the tensor.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns missing validation of a caller-supplied tensor name before deletion; candidate concerns a null pointer check on an allocated memory object.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Trigger is an invalid/missing tensor name; candidate trigger is a failed memory allocation returning NULL.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate shows validating a pointer before use, but does not address name resolution, registry lookup, or deletion eligibility.
audit.reason: Only broad defensive validation theme overlaps; no mechanism-level alignment with session tensor deletion.

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.14.15. There is an array-index-out-of-bounds flaw in the detach_capi_ctr function in drivers/isdn/capi/kcapi.c.

hypothesis.operation: indexing a per-input label-count vector by a fixed input index
hypothesis.trigger_condition: num_inputs is 0 or 1 while the unique-label expression evaluates the second operand
hypothesis.violated_invariant: the fixed input index must be less than num_inputs before indexing input_label_counts
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The unique-label expression can index input_label_counts[0] or [1] when the corresponding input vector does not exist.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard each fixed input index with a num_inputs bound before accessing input_label_counts.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether num_inputs is guaranteed at least 2 before the unique expression or whether short-circuiting prevents the out-of-range index.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both are fixed-index array accesses without validating the index against the actual container size.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis: input_label_counts[0]/[1] may be indexed when num_inputs < 2; candidate: capi_controller[ctr->cnr - 1] indexed without checking cnr bounds.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate directly shows the same repair pattern: guard the fixed index with a bound check before array access.
audit.reason: Strict same failed safety condition: unchecked fixed index into an array.

candidate.cve_desc: Multiple stack-based buffer overflows in the magicmouse_raw_event function in drivers/hid/hid-magicmouse.c in the Magic Mouse HID driver in the Linux kernel through 3.16.3 allow physically proximate attackers to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted device that provides a large amount of (1) EHCI or (2) XHCI data associated with an event.

hypothesis.operation: indexing a label-count vector by a mapped label value
hypothesis.trigger_condition: MapToLabels produces a label value outside [0, num_labels)
hypothesis.violated_invariant: every mapped label must be a valid index into the label-count vectors sized by label_mapping.size()
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: A mapped label value can exceed the label-count vector capacity if label_mapping size does not cover all emitted labels.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Validate or clamp mapped label values against the label-count vector size before incrementing counts.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Inspect MapToLabels to confirm that every returned label is less than label_mapping.size() and that kEllipsisLabel is excluded from count indexing.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis is out-of-range index into label-count vector; candidate is stack buffer overflow due to unchecked npoints.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis trigger is mapped label outside [0, num_labels); candidate trigger is npoints > 15.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate validates a computed count against a fixed capacity before use, which is a concrete transferable principle for validating mapped labels against vector size.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but candidate provides a concrete capacity-validation principle applicable to the hypothesis.

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in fs/xfs/libxfs/xfs_inode_buf.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3. A denial of service (memory corruption and BUG) can occur for a corrupted xfs image upon encountering an inode that is in extent format, but has more extents than fit in the inode fork.

hypothesis.operation: resizing a label-count vector using the label mapping cardinality
hypothesis.trigger_condition: output labels include a value not represented in label_mapping.size()
hypothesis.violated_invariant: num_labels must equal the maximum label index plus one for all later label indexing
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The count vector size derived from map cardinality may not match the label index domain used later.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Derive count vector capacity from the maximum assigned label plus one rather than map size.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Verify that label_mapping assigns dense integer labels so that size equals the valid label index extent.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns a label-count vector sized by map cardinality vs. label index domain; candidate refactors inode fork verification into a helper.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis trigger is an output label not represented in label_mapping.size(); candidate trigger is a corrupted XFS inode with invalid fork format/extent counts.
audit.transferable_principle: No concrete verification or repair principle transfers from inode fork validation to label-count sizing.
audit.reason: Only broad validation/consistency theme overlaps; mechanisms are unrelated.

candidate.cve_desc: Array index error in the MidiManagerUsb::DispatchSendMidiData function in media/midi/midi_manager_usb.cc in Google Chrome before 41.0.2272.76 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging renderer access to provide an invalid port index that triggers an out-of-bounds write operation, a different vulnerability than CVE-2015-1212.

hypothesis.operation: Indexing a NodeDef input vector by a fixed per-op position
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The apply-gradient node has fewer inputs than the fixed position for its op
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The node's input count must exceed the op-specific gradient input index before dereferencing it
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The fixed gradient_pos index may exceed the actual input vector extent for a malformed or unexpected apply-gradient node.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the input access by checking the node's input size against the op-specific index before reading or rewriting it.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether NodeDef input_size is validated against gradient_pos for each apply_gradients_op before the input call.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve indexing a container/vector by an index that may exceed its actual size, with the fix adding a bounds check before access.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis: fixed gradient_pos index may exceed NodeDef input_size. Candidate: renderer-provided port_index may exceed output_streams_.size().
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate repair directly demonstrates checking the index against the container size before dereferencing, matching the hypothesis's requested guard.
audit.reason: Strict same immediate failed safety condition: unchecked index into a container before access.

candidate.cve_desc: An invalid memory access flaw is present in libyang before v1.0-r3 in the function resolve_feature_value() when an if-feature statement is used inside a bit. Applications that use libyang to parse untrusted input yang files may crash.

hypothesis.operation: Dereferencing a possibly uninitialized dequeue node pointer
hypothesis.trigger_condition: ComputeTransitiveFanin returns input nodes while no train node is a dequeue op
hypothesis.violated_invariant: dequeue_node must be initialized before any comparison using its name
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The code compares input_node to dequeue_node without ensuring dequeue_node was assigned when input_nodes is populated.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Initialize dequeue_node to null and guard the input-node loop on its presence before dereferencing it.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Determine whether input_nodes can be nonempty when the dequeue_node search over train_nodes finds no match.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns an uninitialized pointer dereference in TensorFlow; candidate concerns an invalid memory access from missing feature-array check in libyang.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Trigger is absence of a matching dequeue node; candidate trigger is an if-feature inside a bit with empty features array.
audit.transferable_principle: No concrete transferable verification principle for pointer initialization or dequeue-node presence is supplied.
audit.reason: Only broad invalid-memory-access theme overlaps; no mechanism-level alignment.

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in Ceph through 13.2.9. A POST request with an invalid tagging XML can crash the RGW process by triggering a NULL pointer exception.

hypothesis.operation: Map lookup followed by pointer dereference for a node name
hypothesis.risk_object: all_nodes_ map entry and NodeDef pointer
hypothesis.trigger_condition: apply_gradients_nodes_ contains a name absent from all_nodes_ or mapped to null
hypothesis.violated_invariant: Every name in apply_gradients_nodes_ must exist in all_nodes_ with a valid NodeDef pointer before dereferencing
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The operator[] lookup may create or return an invalid entry if the node name is missing, causing a null or invalid NodeDef dereference.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Use a checked find or verify the map entry exists and is non-null before dereferencing the NodeDef pointer.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Verify that every name inserted into apply_gradients_nodes_ is also present in all_nodes_ with a non-null NodeDef.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve dereferencing a pointer obtained from a lookup without checking for NULL: target map lookup then NodeDef dereference; candidate parser.find_first then tagging dereference.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger is missing or null map entry for a node name; candidate trigger is missing Tagging element in XML. Both violate the invariant that the looked-up pointer must be non-null before dereference.
audit.transferable_principle: Check the result of a lookup for NULL before dereferencing it.
audit.reason: Candidate repair adds a NULL check after a lookup before dereference, directly matching the hypothesis's failed safety condition.

candidate.cve_desc: The ReadXWDImage function in coders\xwd.c in ImageMagick 7.0.5-6 has a memory leak vulnerability that can cause memory exhaustion via a crafted length (number of color-map entries) field in the header of an XWD file.

hypothesis.operation: Allocate a row buffer sized by the product of the row stride and a fixed element size.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: MATLAB_HDR.SizeX is large enough that ldblk * sizeof(double) overflows size_t or exceeds available memory.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The computed allocation extent must remain within the process address space and available memory before allocation.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The row stride is multiplied by a fixed element size without proving the product remains a valid allocation extent.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Bound the stride-derived allocation extent before allocating the row buffer.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether SizeX, sample_size, and the allocation size are validated against a maximum before AcquireQuantumMemory.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis is size_t overflow in row buffer allocation; candidate is memory exhaustion from unchecked color-map length in XWD.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve an unchecked size/count used in allocation, though target is multiplication overflow and candidate is excessive length.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate concretely checks length against (~0UL)/sizeof(*colors) before AcquireQuantumMemory, a directly transferable overflow-bound verification principle.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but candidate provides a concrete allocation-size overflow check transferable to the hypothesis.

candidate.cve_desc: A stack-based buffer over-read in the ParseRiffHeaderConfig function of cli/riff.c file of WavPack 5.1.0 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial-of-service attack or possibly have unspecified other impact via a maliciously crafted RF64 file.

hypothesis.operation: Read a row of raster data into the row buffer using the computed row stride.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: ldblk is larger than the actual remaining blob extent or larger than the allocated buffer extent.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The read amount must not exceed both the source blob remaining extent and the destination buffer capacity.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The row read uses a stride-derived amount without proving the destination buffer and source blob can supply that many bytes.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the row read by comparing the stride against the allocated buffer and remaining blob extent.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Verify whether ldblk is constrained by the allocated BImgBuff size and by the remaining bytes in image2 before ReadBlob.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Candidate fixes a read size mismatch by using the destination buffer size instead of an untrusted chunk size, similar to guarding a read by buffer capacity.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Candidate trigger is chunk_header.ckSize larger than destination buffer; hypothesis trigger is ldblk larger than buffer or remaining blob.
audit.transferable_principle: Concrete principle: bound read size by the destination buffer capacity rather than an untrusted length field.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but provides a transferable repair principle for extent validation.

candidate.cve_desc: Array index error in smal_decode_segment function in LibRaw before 0.17.1 allows context-dependent attackers to cause memory errors and possibly execute arbitrary code via vectors related to indexes.

hypothesis.operation: Access an image row by a computed row index and width.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: MATLAB_HDR.SizeY or image->columns is inconsistent with the allocated image extent.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The row index and width must lie within the image's allocated pixel extent before pixel access.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The pixel row access indexes the image using header-derived dimensions without proving they match the allocated image extent.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Validate the header dimensions against the image extent before accessing pixels.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether SetImageExtent guarantees image->rows and image->columns match SizeY and SizeX before GetAuthenticPixels.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns header-derived dimensions not matching allocated image extent before pixel access; candidate checks pix index against raw_width*raw_height before array write.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve using computed indices/dimensions without proving they lie within allocated extent.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate demonstrates bounds check against allocated extent before access, transferable to validating header dimensions before GetAuthenticPixels.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but concrete transferable bounds-checking principle.

candidate.cve_desc: GPAC through 0.7.1 has a Buffer Overflow in the gf_media_avc_read_sps function in media_tools/av_parsers.c, a different vulnerability than CVE-2018-1000100.

hypothesis.operation: Indexing the fixed attribute array msg->attr while parsing attributes
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The input buffer contains more than the fixed number of attributes allowed by msg->attr, causing msg->attr_count to reach the array limit before msg_len becomes zero.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: msg->attr_count must remain below the declared capacity of msg->attr before each write to msg->attr[msg->attr_count].
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The parser increments msg->attr_count and indexes msg->attr without a visible bound check against the array capacity.
hypothesis.repair_sought: A guard that rejects or stops parsing when msg->attr_count reaches the maximum attribute count before indexing msg->attr.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check the definition of pjstun_msg to determine the size of attr and whether any caller or macro enforces the limit before this loop.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve indexing a fixed-capacity array with a count read from input without a bound check against actual capacity.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Trigger is input causing count to exceed array capacity before indexing; candidate checks layer_count against ARRAY_LENGTH before loop.
audit.transferable_principle: Directly transferable: validate parsed count against array capacity before indexing.
audit.reason: Same failed safety condition: missing capacity bound before indexing fixed array.

candidate.cve_desc: GnuTLS before 2017-02-20 has an out-of-bounds write caused by an integer overflow and heap-based buffer overflow related to the cdk_pkt_read function in opencdk/read-packet.c. This issue (which is a subset of the vendor's GNUTLS-SA-2017-3 report) is fixed in 3.5.10.

hypothesis.operation: Computing the aligned attribute length from a parsed 16-bit length field
hypothesis.risk_object: len value used to advance p_attr and decrement msg_len
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The parsed length field is large enough that adding sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr) and then aligning to four bytes overflows pj_uint32_t or produces a value inconsistent with the remaining msg_len.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The computed aligned len must not overflow and must represent a valid extent within the remaining message length before p_attr is advanced.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The attribute length is computed by adding a parsed field to a constant and aligning, which can overflow or create an invalid extent before the msg_len < len check.
hypothesis.repair_sought: A check that the parsed length plus header size and alignment does not exceed a safe maximum before using len to advance the cursor.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Verify whether the parsed length field is bounded and whether the addition and alignment can wrap on the target platform.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve integer overflow in length/size arithmetic leading to out-of-bounds access, but the candidate's overflow is in packet length accumulation during parsing, not in adding a header size and aligning an attribute length.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Candidate enforces a maximum packet length before using it in calculations; hypothesis requires bounding parsed length plus header and alignment before advancing a cursor. The invariant is similar (safe extent before use) but the exact trigger and arithmetic differ.
audit.transferable_principle: The candidate demonstrates the concrete principle of validating a parsed length against a safe maximum before using it in size calculations, which directly supports the hypothesis's requested repair.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure (packet length accumulation vs attribute length alignment) but provides a transferable verification/repair principle for bounding parsed lengths before arithmetic.

candidate.cve_desc: drivers/staging/ozwpan/ozusbsvc1.c in the OZWPAN driver in the Linux kernel through 4.0.5 does not ensure that certain length values are sufficiently large, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (system crash or large loop) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted packet, related to the (1) oz_usb_rx and (2) oz_usb_handle_ep_data functions.

hypothesis.operation: Comparing the parsed message length against the buffer length minus the header size
hypothesis.trigger_condition: buf_len is smaller than sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr), causing buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) to underflow as an unsigned value and making the length comparison pass incorrectly.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: buf_len must be at least sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) before subtracting the header size from buf_len.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The header size is subtracted from buf_len without a visible check that buf_len is large enough, which can underflow and bypass the length validation.
hypothesis.repair_sought: A guard that rejects buffers smaller than the header size before computing buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr).
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether callers or prior validation ensure buf_len is at least sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr before this function executes.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns unsigned underflow when subtracting header size from buf_len without ensuring buf_len is large enough; candidate adds length check before subtraction.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve length arithmetic where insufficient length causes underflow or invalid computation.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate demonstrates guarding length before subtraction to prevent underflow, directly transferable to checking buf_len >= sizeof(header) before buf_len - sizeof(header).
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but concrete transferable length-underflow prevention principle.

candidate.cve_desc: An integer overflow in the search_in_range function in regexec.c in Oniguruma 6.x before 6.9.4_rc2 leads to an out-of-bounds read, in which the offset of this read is under the control of an attacker. (This only affects the 32-bit compiled version). Remote attackers can cause a denial-of-service or information disclosure, or possibly have unspecified other impact, via a crafted regular expression.

hypothesis.operation: Compute and store the body start offset after consuming the final CRLF.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The final CRLF is the last two bytes of the buffer, so p points to the final byte and p - buffer + 1 equals len.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: body_start must remain strictly less than len so later body reads have a valid in-buffer offset.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The +1 offset arithmetic can produce a body_start equal to the buffer length when the header ends exactly at the buffer end.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Clamp or validate the computed body_start against len before storing it.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether the final CRLF can be the last two bytes and whether body_start == len is handled safely by consumers.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Candidate involves integer overflow in regex range arithmetic, not offset arithmetic producing body_start == len.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Trigger is crafted regex causing integer overflow; hypothesis trigger is final CRLF at buffer end causing body_start == len.
audit.transferable_principle: No concrete transferable verification or repair principle for validating body_start against len.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure and no mechanism-level alignment.

candidate.cve_desc: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in GnuTLS. As Nettle's hash update functions internally call memcpy, providing zero-length input may cause undefined behavior. This flaw leads to a denial of service after authentication in rare circumstances.

hypothesis.operation: Pass the remaining buffer extent to the header_done callback.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The final CRLF is the last two bytes, so p points to the final byte and pe - p - 1 is zero.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The callback must receive a nonnegative remaining extent and a valid pointer within the buffer.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The computed remaining extent can be zero when the header ends at the buffer end, which may be outside the callback's expected domain.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the header_done call so the remaining extent is nonnegative and the pointer is valid.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether pe - p - 1 can be zero and whether header_done handles zero-length remaining data.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns zero-length remaining extent passed to callback; candidate guards zero-length input to hash update.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve zero-length data causing undefined behavior or invalid domain use.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate demonstrates guarding zero-length input before invoking a function that may not handle it, directly relevant to checking header_done with zero remaining extent.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but concrete transferable principle for zero-length input validation.

candidate.cve_desc: drivers/media/usb/dvb-usb/cxusb.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x and 4.10.x before 4.10.12 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a DMA scatterlist.

hypothesis.operation: Mutate the current input byte in place while parsing.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The caller supplies a read-only or shared buffer that must not be modified.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: The buffer must be writable before in-place mutation.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: In-place mutation of the input buffer can corrupt read-only or shared data if the caller does not own a writable copy.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Ensure the buffer is writable or copy it before mutation.

candidate.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.MaxPoolGradWithArgmax` can cause reads outside of bounds of heap allocated data if attacker supplies specially crafted inputs. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/31bd5026304677faa8a0b77602c6154171b9aec1/tensorflow/core/kernels/image/draw_bounding_box_op.cc#L116-L130) assumes that the last element of `boxes` input is 4, as required by [the op](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/DrawBoundingBoxesV2). Since this is not checked attackers passing values less than 4 can write outside of bounds of heap allocated objects and cause memory corruption. If the last dimension in `boxes` is less than 4, accesses similar to `tboxes(b, bb, 3)` will access data outside of bounds. Further during code execution there are also writes to these indices. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

hypothesis.violated_invariant: vrp and vrp->vdev must remain valid and owned by the caller for the lifetime of the embedded device
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The parent pointer is set from vrp->vdev without a local check that vrp and vdev are valid and still owned.
hypothesis.repair_sought: A guard or ownership invariant ensuring vrp and vrp->vdev remain valid before parent assignment and registration.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether the caller guarantees vrp and vrp->vdev are non-NULL and not concurrently released before this function runs.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns missing validity/ownership check on vrp/vdev before parent pointer assignment; candidate fixes NULL dereference of sprinc in krb5 realm setup.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve NULL pointer dereference, but the objects and invariants differ (rpmsg device parent vs. realm principal).
audit.transferable_principle: Generic defensive NULL check before dereference; no specific mechanism-level guidance for the rpmsg ownership invariant.
audit.reason: Only broad NULL-pointer/CWE-476 theme overlaps; no concrete transferable verification principle for the hypothesis.

candidate.cve_desc: The grub_ext2_read_block function in fs/ext2.c in GNU GRUB before 2013-11-12, as used in shlr/grub/fs/ext2.c in radare2 1.5.0, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive stack use and application crash) via a crafted binary file, related to use of a variable-size stack array.

hypothesis.operation: Register an embedded rpmsg_device whose release callback may free the containing vch
hypothesis.trigger_condition: registration succeeds or fails in a way that transfers or releases ownership of the embedded device before the caller can manage vch

hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The embedded device is registered without a locally visible ownership contract for the containing vch allocation.
hypothesis.repair_sought: An ownership or reference-count invariant clarifying whether registration takes ownership of the embedded device or only borrows it.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Inspect rpmsg_ctrldev_register_device and virtio_rpmsg_release_device to determine whether vch is freed on success, failure, or later release.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis concerns ownership transfer of embedded rpmsg device; candidate fixes stack buffer allocation and missing frees in ext2 block reading.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Hypothesis trigger is registration ownership transfer; candidate trigger is crafted ext2 filesystem causing stack overuse.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate's memory management fixes do not provide a concrete ownership/reference-count verification principle for the rpmsg registration hypothesis.
audit.reason: No mechanism-level alignment with ownership transfer hypothesis.

candidate.cve_desc: The ReadVIFFImage function in coders/viff.c in ImageMagick before 7.0.1-0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or have other unspecified impact via a crafted file.

hypothesis.operation: Read colormap bytes into a heap buffer allocated for image->colors entries
hypothesis.trigger_condition: image->colors is large enough that packet_size*image->colors overflows size_t or exceeds the allocated extent
hypothesis.violated_invariant: packet_size*image->colors must not overflow and must equal the allocated buffer size
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The colormap read length is computed by multiplying image->colors by packet_size, which can overflow or exceed the allocated buffer extent.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the multiplication against overflow and verify the resulting length matches the allocated colormap buffer size.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether image->colors is bounded before the multiplication and whether the allocation size equals packet_size*image->colors.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Hypothesis claims size/offset arithmetic overflow in colormap read length; candidate fixes size arithmetic overflow in VIFF packet count computation.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve attacker-controlled dimensions causing multiplication overflow before allocation/read, though target is colormap read and candidate is pixel packet allocation.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate's CheckMemoryOverflow guard before multiplication is a concrete transferable verification principle for the hypothesis's requested overflow guard.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure, but the overflow-check-before-multiplication repair principle directly helps assess the hypothesis.

candidate.cve_desc: Buffer overflow in coders/tiff.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.5-1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or have other unspecified impact via a crafted file.

hypothesis.operation: Compute total pixel buffer length from bytes_per_line and image->rows
hypothesis.risk_object: length value used for ReadBlob and AcquireVirtualMemory
hypothesis.trigger_condition: bytes_per_line*image->rows overflows size_t or exceeds the allocated virtual memory extent
hypothesis.violated_invariant: bytes_per_line*image->rows must not overflow and must fit within the allocated pixel buffer
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: The pixel buffer length is computed by multiplying bytes_per_line by image->rows, which can overflow or exceed the allocated buffer extent.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the multiplication against overflow and verify the resulting length matches the allocated pixel buffer size.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether bytes_per_line and image->rows are bounded before the multiplication and whether the allocation size equals length.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both concern size/offset arithmetic for pixel buffers where multiplication can overflow or exceed the allocated extent, leading to buffer overflow.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: The candidate replaces a flawed overflow check with HeapOverflowSanityCheck and uses AcquireQuantumMemory with separate dimensions; the hypothesis requires guarding bytes_per_line*image->rows against overflow and matching allocation size. The invariant (product must not overflow and must fit allocation) aligns closely.
audit.transferable_principle: The candidate provides a concrete repair pattern: use a heap overflow sanity check on the row count and allocate with separate column/row factors to avoid overflow.
audit.reason: Same immediate failed safety condition: unchecked size multiplication used for allocation/read extent, with a directly transferable overflow-check repair.

candidate.cve_desc: decode_frame in libavcodec/exr.c in FFmpeg 4.3.1 has an out-of-bounds write because of errors in calculations of when to perform memset zero operations.

hypothesis.operation: Index into the pixel buffer using a row offset computed from image->rows, y, and bytes_per_line

hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether the allocated pixel buffer size is at least image->rows*bytes_per_line and whether the row offset stays within that bound.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve out-of-bounds access due to incorrect extent calculations, but target is a row offset into a pixel buffer while candidate is a memset loop over rows beyond image height.

audit.reason: Different immediate failure (row offset indexing vs memset loop) but provides a concrete verification principle for bounding row-based accesses.

candidate.cve_desc: The grub_memmove function in shlr/grub/kern/misc.c in radare2 1.5.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted binary file, possibly related to a read overflow in the grub_disk_read_small_real function in kern/disk.c in GNU GRUB 2.02.

audit.transferable_principle: Candidate directly demonstrates bounding a copy against the known buffer size before memcpy.
audit.reason: Same failed safety condition: unchecked offset/length before memory copy causing out-of-bounds read.

candidate.cve_desc: Buffer overflow in virtio_net_load function in net/virtio-net.c in QEMU 1.3.0 through 1.7.x before 1.7.2 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a large MAC table.

audit.root_cause_alignment: The hypothesis concerns a parser cursor dereferencing payload beyond a fixed header without validating the total variable payload extent against the request length; the candidate also addresses missing length checks before parsing variable-length data, but in a different protocol and with different immediate failure.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Both involve a too-short message relative to the required per-bit or per-field data, but the candidate's checks are for Bluetooth AVRCP message lengths rather than X11 request length versus affectWhich bits.
audit.transferable_principle: Validate that the declared message length covers all variable-length fields before advancing or dereferencing the payload cursor.

candidate.cve_desc: Buffer overflow in the mainloop function in nbd-server.c in the server in Network Block Device (nbd) before 2.9.20 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long request.  NOTE: this issue exists because of a CVE-2005-3534 regression.

hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Verify that size * 2 matches the actual bytes consumed for each case and that dataLeft covers all remaining elements.

audit.transferable_principle: Ensure that bounds checks account for all components of the data being written or read, including headers or trailers, to prevent overflow.
audit.reason: The candidate provides a concrete transferable principle of correcting a bounds check to include all relevant sizes, though the immediate failure differs (per-element vs. total request).

For Openssl 1.0.2, the crash can be triggered when using RC4-MD5; users who have not disabled that algorithm should update to 1.0.2k.

hypothesis.operation: trailing payload length check after parsing

hypothesis.mechanism_claim: Unsigned subtraction of payload sizes from dataLeft can underflow if the required extent is not correctly bounded, producing a wrong remaining length.
hypothesis.repair_sought: A repair that ensures dataLeft cannot underflow by validating the total required extent before subtraction.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check the type of dataLeft and whether all subtractions are guarded against underflow.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve length/offset arithmetic on remaining buffer size, but the candidate's immediate failure is a missing lower-bound check before subtracting a digest length, not an unsigned underflow of a remaining-length variable.

audit.transferable_principle: The candidate demonstrates the concrete principle of validating a length before subtracting a fixed extent to prevent underflow/negative remaining length, which is directly transferable to assessing the hypothesis.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure (missing lower-bound check vs unsigned underflow) but supplies a concrete transferable verification principle for length-before-subtraction validation.

candidate.cve_desc: Format string vulnerability in the extractPages function in utils/pdfseparate.cc in poppler before 0.24.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via format string specifiers in a destination filename.

hypothesis.operation: Initialize a variable-argument list twice before formatting it into a fixed buffer.
hypothesis.trigger_condition: The second va_start overwrites the first initialization, leaving the first va_list state unused and potentially invalidating the expected argument-transfer contract.
hypothesis.violated_invariant: A va_list must be initialized exactly once before use and not reinitialized while the first list is still considered active.
hypothesis.mechanism_claim: Duplicate va_start calls can leave the variable-argument list in an undefined or inconsistent state before vsnprintf consumes it.
hypothesis.repair_sought: Use a single va_start before vsnprintf and a matching va_end.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether the duplicate va_start is reachable and whether the resulting va_list is used by vsnprintf without reinitialization.

hypothesis.repair_sought: Guard the backward scan so it can safely fall back when no whitespace is found before the buffer start.
hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Determine whether ptr[cut] can be accessed for all cut values and whether a missing whitespace leaves ptr and len in a consistent state.

audit.transferable_principle: Check the next/previous character before dereferencing or advancing a parser cursor at a boundary.
audit.reason: Different immediate failure but concrete boundary-check principle transfers to the wrap scan.

hypothesis.evidence_to_check: Check whether len can exceed sizeof(print_buffer) and whether ptr advances only within the stored bytes.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both involve using a length/return value from a formatting function without ensuring it does not exceed the actual buffer capacity, but the candidate's root cause is a truncated path leading to wrong file access, not an OOB read from a fixed buffer.

audit.reason: Different immediate failure (truncated path vs. OOB read from print_buffer) but the candidate provides a concrete, transferable return-value-vs-buffer-size check principle.

In the worst case scenario, by sending specially-crafted WiFi packets, a remote, unauthenticated attacker may be able to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable system. hypothesis.violated_invariant: k must remain less than the number of cp950_pua_tbl entries before cp950_pua_tbl[k] is read

candidate.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.MaxPoolGradWithArgmax` can cause reads outside of bounds of heap allocated data if attacker supplies specially crafted inputs. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/31bd5026304677faa8a0b77602c6154171b9aec1/tensorflow/core/kernels/image/draw_bounding_box_op.cc#L116-L130) assumes that the last element of `boxes` input is 4, as required by [the op](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/DrawBoundingBoxesV2). Since this is not checked attackers passing values less than 4 can write outside of bounds of heap allocated objects and cause memory corruption. If the last dimension in `boxes` is less than 4, accesses similar to `tboxes(b, bb, 3)` will access data outside of bounds. Further during code execution there are also writes to these indices. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

All OpenSSL 1.1.1 versions are affected by this issue. Users of these versions should upgrade to OpenSSL 1.1.1k. OpenSSL 1.0.2 is not impacted by this issue. candidate.cve_desc: Heap-based buffer overflow in the PushQuantumPixel function in ImageMagick before 6.9.7-3 and 7.x before 7.0.4-3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted TIFF file.

target.cve_desc: In Exiv2 0.26, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the Exiv2::Image::byteSwap4 function in image.cpp. Remote attackers can exploit this vulnerability to disclose memory data or cause a denial of service via a crafted TIFF file.

target.cve_desc: In drivers/hid/hid-elo.c in the Linux kernel before 5.16.11, a memory leak exists for a certain hid_parse error condition.

candidate.cve_desc: Use-after-free vulnerability in Google Chrome before 13.0.782.107 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via vectors related to the frame loader.

target.cve_desc: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions TensorFlow's Grappler optimizer has a use of unitialized variable. audit.root_cause_alignment: Target: uninitialized variable. Candidate: use-after-free and logic changes in sync code. No alignment.

target.cve_desc: xmlparse.c in Expat (aka libexpat) before 2.4.5 allows attackers to insert namespace-separator characters into namespace URIs.

audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger is namespace separator character in URI; candidate trigger is invalid grouping character/length combination.

candidate.cve_desc: A flaw was found in OpenEXR's hufDecode functionality. This flaw allows an attacker who can pass a crafted file to be processed by OpenEXR, to trigger an undefined right shift error. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

target.cve_desc: ntpq in NTP 4.2.x before 4.2.8p4, and 4.3.x before 4.3.77 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via crafted mode 6 response packets.

target.cve_desc: When using certain mbstring functions to convert multibyte encodings, in PHP versions 7.2.x below 7.2.27, 7.3.x below 7.3.14 and 7.4.x below 7.4.2 it is possible to supply data that will cause function mbfl_filt_conv_big5_wchar to read past the allocated buffer. candidate.cve_desc: In the Linux kernel before 5.3.4, there is an info-leak bug that can be caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/media/usb/ttusb-dec/ttusb_dec.c driver, aka CID-a10feaf8c464.

target.cve_desc: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of `AssignOp` can result in copying uninitialized data to a new tensor. The implementation has a check that the left hand side of the assignment is initialized (to minimize number of allocations), but does not check that the right hand side is also initialized. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Target: copying uninitialized data from RHS tensor in AssignOp. Candidate: using kzalloc instead of kmalloc to zero-initialize a buffer in a USB driver.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger: RHS tensor not initialized. Candidate trigger: allocation of a command packet buffer that may be read before initialization.
audit.transferable_principle: Both involve uninitialized data, but the candidate's fix (zero-initialize allocation) is not a verification or repair principle for checking tensor initialization.
audit.reason: Only broad CWE-908 theme overlap; no mechanism-level alignment.

candidate.cve_desc: In FFmpeg 3.3.3, a DoS in cine_read_header() due to lack of an EOF check might cause huge CPU and memory consumption. target.cve_desc: ImageMagick 7.1.0-27 is vulnerable to Buffer Overflow.

target.cve_desc: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in the drill format T-code tool number functionality of Gerbv 2.7.0, dev (commit b5f1eacd), and the forked version of Gerbv (commit 71493260). audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger is a crafted drill file with an out-of-bounds tool number; candidate trigger is a font with CFF2/glyf tables. Different immediate conditions.

candidate.cve_desc: The m_authenticate function in ircd/m_authenticate.c in nefarious2 allows remote attackers to spoof certificate fingerprints and consequently log in as another user via a crafted AUTHENTICATE parameter.

target.cve_desc: The auth component in Dovecot before 2.2.27, when auth-policy is configured, allows a remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) by aborting authentication without setting a username.

audit.root_cause_alignment: The target repair handles a NULL username to avoid a crash; the candidate repair rejects malformed AUTHENTICATE parameters to prevent certificate fingerprint spoofing.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: The target trigger is an authentication abort without a username; the candidate trigger is a crafted AUTHENTICATE parameter containing ':' or space.
audit.transferable_principle: No concrete transferable verification or repair principle for the target's NULL-username crash is provided by the candidate.

candidate.cve_desc: The sdb_set_internal function in sdb.c in radare2 2.7.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid read and application crash) via a crafted ELF file because of missing input validation in r_bin_dwarf_parse_comp_unit in libr/bin/dwarf.c.

target.cve_desc: Rizin is a UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. In versions up to and including 0.3.1 there is a heap-based out of bounds write in parse_die() when reversing an AMD64 ELF binary with DWARF debug info. When a malicious AMD64 ELF binary is opened by a victim user, Rizin may crash or execute unintended actions. No workaround are known and users are advised to upgrade.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Target: heap out-of-bounds write in parse_die due to missing count guard. Candidate: invalid read in DWARF parsing due to missing string pointer validation. Different failure and root cause.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger: abbrev->count zero causing underflow in loop bound. Candidate trigger: invalid string pointer. No overlap.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate's pointer check does not transfer to count/loop-bound validation.
audit.reason: Only broad DWARF parsing theme; no mechanism-level alignment.

candidate.cve_desc: An issue was discovered in PHP 7.x before 7.1.26, 7.2.x before 7.2.14, and 7.3.x before 7.3.2. dns_get_record misparses a DNS response, which can allow a hostile DNS server to cause PHP to misuse memcpy, leading to read operations going past the buffer allocated for DNS data. This affects php_parserr in ext/standard/dns.c for DNS_CAA and DNS_ANY queries.

target.cve_desc: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. A buffer overflow vulnerability in versions 2.12 and prior affects applications that use PJSIP DNS resolution. It doesn't affect PJSIP users who utilize an external resolver. This vulnerability is related to CVE-2023-27585. The difference is that this issue is in parsing the query record `parse_rr()`, while the issue in CVE-2023-27585 is in `parse_query()`. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. A workaround is to disable DNS resolution in PJSIP config (by setting `nameserver_count` to zero) or use an external resolver instead.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Both target and candidate are DNS response parsers that read fixed-size fields from a packet without first verifying that the remaining buffer length covers those fields, leading to out-of-bounds reads.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: In both cases the trigger is a malformed/short DNS response where the parser advances a cursor and dereferences it without checking that the declared or remaining length covers the required fixed fields.
audit.transferable_principle: Before copying or dereferencing fixed-size fields from a network packet, validate that the remaining buffer length is at least the size of those fields.
audit.reason: The candidate repair adds exactly the same kind of length guard before reading fixed-size DNS fields, making it a direct mechanism-level reference for the target's missing bounds check.

candidate.cve_desc: Memory leak in the v9fs_read function in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via vectors related to an I/O read operation.

target.cve_desc: An out-of-bounds read flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s io_uring module in the way a user triggers the io_read() function with some special parameters. This flaw allows a local user to read some memory out of bounds.

audit.root_cause_alignment: Target is an out-of-bounds read in io_uring io_read due to iterator state; candidate is a memory leak in QEMU v9fs_read.
audit.trigger_invariant_alignment: Target trigger involves special io_read parameters and iterator count/truncated state; candidate trigger is an I/O read error path leaking qiov allocations.
audit.transferable_principle: Candidate shows cleanup on error paths, which is unrelated to preventing an out-of-bounds read via iterator re-expansion.
audit.reason: No mechanism-level alignment; only broad I/O read theme overlaps.

candidate.cve_desc: The MScrollV function in ansi.c in GNU screen 4.3.1 and earlier does not properly limit recursion, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack consumption) via an escape sequence with a large repeat count value.

target.cve_desc: vim is vulnerable to Heap-based Buffer Overflow

candidate.cve_desc: The sctp_v6_create_accept_sk function in net/sctp/ipv6.c in the Linux kernel through 4.11.1 mishandles inheritance, which allows local users to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls, a related issue to CVE-2017-8890.

target.cve_desc: Integer overflow in the sctp_setsockopt_auth_key function in net/sctp/socket.c in the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (sctp) implementation in the Linux kernel 2.6.24-rc1 through 2.6.26.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (panic) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted sca_keylength field associated with the SCTP_AUTH_KEY option.

candidate.cve_desc: The fmtstr function in crypto/bio/b_print.c in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1s and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2g improperly calculates string lengths, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (overflow and out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a long string, as demonstrated by a large amount of ASN.1 data, a different vulnerability than CVE-2016-2842.

target.cve_desc: Curl versions 7.14.1 through 7.61.1 are vulnerable to a heap-based buffer over-read in the tool_msgs.c:voutf() function that may result in information exposure and denial of service.
